key_insight: A GPT2 table-to-text approach can outperform traditional ML and neural models for prediction on small, imbalanced clinical datasets by using clinical-language context instead of relying only on statistical patterns.
clinical_relevance: This may help clinicians and researchers build more reliable disease prediction tools from low-volume electronic health record data, especially when positive cases are rare.
method: Converted structured clinical variables into physician-style text.
Used GPT4-based medical paraphrasing to augment minority-class examples.
Fine-tuned GPT2 on four public healthcare datasets and added gradient-based explainability.
evidence_signal: Across heart disease, heart failure, chronic kidney disease, and thyroid cancer recurrence datasets, the model reported average precision 0.96, specificity 0.97, sensitivity 0.96, and F1-score 0.96.
watch_item: Performance was shown on public datasets, so real-world validation and careful checking for synthetic-text bias or leakage would be needed before clinical use.
paper_title: Can GPT Be Used as an Alternative Prediction Model to Traditional Machine Learning and Neural Networks on Low-Volume Clinical Data?
